title: Rigidity of already given coherent relative dualizing pairs
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a separated flat locally finitely presented morphism of schemes with $S$ locally Noetherian [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Put $Y=X\times_SX$ with first projection $p_1$ and closed diagonal $\Delta$. A relative dualizing pair in this statement means a given object $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ which is pseudo-coherent and locally has finite Tor amplitude over $S$, together with a map $\xi:\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\to Lp_1^*K$ such that multiplication by $\xi$ gives an isomorphism $\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_Y(\Delta_*\mathcal O_X,Lp_1^*K)$ [def-pc-derived-category], [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], [def-pc-derived-pullback], [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For any such pair the scalar map $\mathcal O_X\to R\mathcal Hom_X(K,K)$ is an isomorphism. Given two such pairs $(K,\xi)$ and $(L,\eta)$, there is exactly one isomorphism $\alpha:K\to L$ with $(Lp_1^*\alpha)\xi=\eta$. The same assertions apply to any open restriction $U\to S$ of $f$. This statement assumes the pairs are already supplied and asserts no existence of a pair.

source.place: Tags 0E2T (given pair definition), 0E2V (scalar derived endomorphisms), 0E2W (unique class-preserving isomorphism).

proof.text: Take the basis $\mathcal B$ of affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ mapping into affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $S$, choosing the latter inside a Noetherian affine cover. Refine by smaller such opens when necessary. The affine-comparison lemma gives a flat finitely presented map $R\to A$ of Noetherian rings and an algebraic object $M$ for $K|_U$ which is pseudo-coherent, has finite $R$-Tor amplitude, and satisfies $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,M_1)\cong A$ for $B=A\otimes_RA$. Its class $\xi_U$ is a basis of the rank-one $A$-module $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(A,M_1)$. Indeed, taking degree zero in the multiplication isomorphism identifies that Hom group with $A$, sending $1$ to $\xi_U$. Apply the same comparison to any second supplied pair.

For this ring map put $C=\varphi^!R=R\operatorname{Hom}_{P}(A,P)[n]$, where $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$. The algebraic relative-perfection theorem gives pseudo-coherence, finite $R$-Tor amplitude and the scalar isomorphism $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,C)$. Set $p_i:A\to B$ to be the coprojections and $\delta:B\to A$ multiplication. Flat base change in the shriek calculus, for $R\to R'=A$ and input $R[0]\in D^+(R)$, gives $C\otimes_{A,p_1}^{\mathbf L}B\cong p_2^!A$. Composition for $A\xrightarrow{p_2}B\xrightarrow{\delta}A$, whose composite is the identity, gives $\delta^!p_2^!A\cong A$. The surjective-map coinduction clause identifies its underlying $B$-object with $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,C\otimes_{A,p_1}^{\mathbf L}B)$. All these rings are Noetherian finite-type $R$-algebras: apply the Noetherian-algebra theorem to $P,A,B$. Thus $C$ meets every hypothesis of the algebraic isomorphism lemma, without assuming the kernel of $P\to A$ is a regular sequence.

source.place: Tags 0BZW (lemma-relative-dualizing-algebraic) and 0E2E (lemma-relative-dualizing-noetherian), proof via flat base change and composition.

proof.text: The algebraic isomorphism lemma applied to $M,C$ supplies an $A$-linear isomorphism $M\cong C$. Conjugation by it identifies the scalar maps into their derived endomorphism objects, since an $A$-linear isomorphism commutes with multiplication by every $a\in A$. Consequently $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,M)$ is an isomorphism. The affine pseudo-coherent RHom comparison identifies its sheafification with $\mathcal O_U\to R\mathcal Hom_U(K|_U,K|_U)$: its first argument has a bounded-above finite-free representative, and its second is bounded below because finite $R$-Tor amplitude applied to $R$ gives bounded cohomology. Derived internal Hom commutes with open restriction, so the restriction to every $U\in\mathcal B$ of the global scalar map is an isomorphism. The cone has zero cohomology sheaves on this covering, hence zero cohomology sheaves globally. This proves the first assertion.

source.place: Tag 0E2V, lemma-relative-dualizing-RHom, via the Noetherian algebraic argument of 0E2G; affine RHom comparison 0A6H.

proof.text: Now let $(K,\xi),(L,\eta)$ be supplied pairs. On $U\in\mathcal B$ the algebraic isomorphism lemma and affine derived equivalence supply an isomorphism $\beta_U:K|_U\to L|_U$. Its action sends the generator $\xi_U$ to another generator of the $A$-module $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(A,L_1)$. Hence $\beta_U(\xi_U)=u\eta_U$ for a unique unit $u\in A^\times$. Define $\alpha_U=u^{-1}\beta_U$; its derived pullback sends $\xi_U$ to $\eta_U$. Any automorphism of $K|_U$ is a scalar unit: by step 3 its derived endomorphism object is $A$, so its degree-zero endomorphism ring is $A$. If it fixes $\xi_U$, multiplication on the free rank-one class module forces that unit to be $1$. Thus $\alpha_U$ is the unique class-preserving isomorphism. The same scalar computation gives $\operatorname{Hom}(K|_U,K|_U[i])=0$ for every $i<0$.

source.place: Tag 0E2W, lemma-uniqueness-relative-dualizing, first two paragraphs; affine normalization and scalar automorphisms.

proof.text: For an inclusion $W\subset U$ of basis elements, $\alpha_U|_W$ and $\alpha_W$ preserve the restricted class, so they agree by the affine uniqueness of step 4. Use the BBD descent theorem with local objects $K_U=K|_U$ and their canonical restriction isomorphisms. Its negative self-extension hypothesis is exactly the last conclusion of step 4. The global object $K$ with identity local identifications is one solution, while $L$ with identifications $\alpha_U^{-1}:L|_U\to K_U$ is another; the just-proved inclusion compatibility verifies its descent condition. The uniqueness clause of that theorem gives an isomorphism $\alpha:K\to L$ whose restrictions are $\alpha_U$. This uses a basis, not a finite cover; intersections are only required to be unions of smaller basis elements. No quasi-compactness or affine-intersection assumption is made.

source.place: Tag 0E2W, final paragraph; Cohomology Tags 0D67 and 0D6C, uniqueness clause of BBD descent.

proof.text: The multiplication isomorphism belonging to $(L,\eta)$, together with the derived-Hom/global-sections identity, identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_Y)}(\Delta_*\mathcal O_X,Lp_1^*L)$ with $H^0(Y,\Delta_*\mathcal O_X)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, sending $\eta$ to $1$. Thus $(Lp_1^*\alpha)\xi$ is $v\eta$ for one global function $v$. Its restriction along every $U$ is $\eta_U$, by the construction of $\alpha_U$, so $v|_U=1$ for all $U$. The sheaf axiom gives $v=1$, proving class preservation globally. To check uniqueness, let $\alpha'$ be any other class-preserving isomorphism. Its restriction to every basis open equals $\alpha_U$ by step 4. In the BBD system of step 5 both $\alpha$ and $\alpha'$ respect all local identifications, so its unique-isomorphism clause gives $\alpha'=\alpha$. The global-sections computation also rules out an undetected class difference away from the diagonal, whose derived Hom object is supported on $\Delta(X)$.

source.place: Tag 0E2W, normalization and last sentence; Cohomology derived-Hom/global-sections identity.

proof.text: Finally let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be any open, including the empty open. Pseudo-coherence and the local relative Tor bounds remain true upon restricting their local representatives. For the square of diagonals, the inverse image of $U\times_SU$ under $\Delta$ is $U$, so restriction of $\Delta_*\mathcal O_X$ is $\Delta_{U*}\mathcal O_U$ directly from the definition of closed-immersion direct image. Derived pullback and derived internal Hom commute with this open restriction, so the restricted class still satisfies the multiplication isomorphism. The morphism $f|_U$ is separated, flat and locally finitely presented, as is checked on the same charts (its diagonal is the restricted closed immersion). The base $S$ is unchanged. Repeating steps 1--6 for the supplied restricted pairs proves both assertions on $U$. For $U=\varnothing$ all module sheaves and all objects and maps are zero, so the conclusions hold as well.
